title: Salmonella Turned Into Cancer Killing Super Bug
main_content:
Not many people consider a bacterium that makes millions of people sick a friend. But scientist Roy Curtiss does.

Roy Curtiss is a microbiologist at the Biodesign Institute at Arizona State University. He uses the word ‘bug,’ a common expression for a germ or virus, when talking about Salmonella bacteria.

Salmonella is the most common bacteria to harm, or contaminate, food. It is found in undercooked meats, eggs and milk. Salmonella can cause a higher than normal body temperature and pain in the abdomen. The person may feel sick.

Millions of people are sickened each year by Salmonella. But a genetically-engineered version of the bacteria may someday be used as a weapon against cancer. As the old saying goes, “The enemy of my enemy is my friend.”

Researchers in the United States and Germany have turned Salmonella into a weapon against cancerous tumors. Roy Curtiss says the bacteria can make the cancer cells disappear.

questions.question: Who is Roy Curtiss?
options: A renowned chef specializing in meat dishes
A microbiologist at the Biodesign Institute at Arizona State University
A researcher in the field of dietary medicine
questions.answer: A microbiologist at the Biodesign Institute at Arizona State University

questions.question: What does the word ‘bug’ mean?
options: A term used for an insect
A common expression for a germ or virus
A nickname for a viral infection
A reference to a software error
questions.answer: A common expression for a germ or virus

questions.question: Where can you find Salmonella?
options: In undercooked meats, eggs, and milk
questions.answer: In undercooked meats, eggs, and milk
